A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-C are readable and can be matched despite pagination and figure rearrangements.

before.justification: Section 6 and Table 1 report original ImageNet-1K experiments on equivariant and hybrid networks, including classification accuracy, throughput and memory measurements.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Table 1 additionally reports results for three halfway-invariantized I(ViT) models.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 adds I(ViT): halfway through the network, it discards the sign-changing features, linearly expands d/2 invariant dimensions to d dimensions, and continues with ordinary ViT layers. The existing equivariant and hybrid architectures are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate supervised ImageNet-1K image classification. I(ViT) adds model variants within this coverage; discussion of other symmetry groups does not introduce evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds I(ViT-B), I(ViT-L) and I(ViT-H) as internal comparison methods alongside the fully equivariant and hybrid ViTs. The existing ResMLP, DeiT III and ConvNeXt comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new I(ViT) experiments add invariant-only second-half controls at B/L/H scales, with the same reported parameter and FLOP budgets as corresponding H(ViT) models. Existing training recipes, model dimensions, metrics and throughput procedures remain unchanged in Appendices B and Tables 2-3.

E4.justification: The I(ViT) comparison tests the choice of intermediate group representations by enforcing invariance halfway through the network. Section 4.2, Table 1 and Figure 5 add this architectural analysis beyond v1's fully equivariant and hybrid comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions state one training per model and mention unsuccessful E(ViT-S) attempts with different seeds. Appendix B retains throughput averaging over 100 runs after 10 warm-up iterations. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds I(ViT-B/L/H) top-1 accuracies of 82.5%, 84.1% and 84.7%, respectively, plus their efficiency measurements. All 25 pre-existing result rows retain their values; these are additional model results, not improved scores for existing models.

T1.justification: Appendix A's Lemma A.2 drops the finite-group assumption. New Section 3.6 explicitly discusses generalization under complete reducibility, although much of its computational interpretation already appeared in v1's Appendix A. The other formal results and Appendix C derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central contribution: flopping-equivariant networks achieve comparable FLOPs per parameter, approximately halve FLOPs, and improve throughput while remaining competitive at larger scales. Small modal edits do not redefine the headline contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 adds counterevidence concerning learned weight symmetries and explicitly calls learning equivariance from symmetric data unsettled. Its expressivity argument changes from 'since' equivariance is learned to 'if' it is learned. Existing experimental limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 replaces a generic promise of release on GitHub with a specific repository address for code and weights. It still describes a future release. Appendix B's software, hardware, training-time and measurement details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds brief coverage of steerable-filter history, canonicalization, learned equivariance, structured matrices and newer point-cloud work. Section 3.5 adds Moskalev et al.; Appendix A replaces Boardman with the already-cited Serre. The central positioning around computational efficiency remains.

P1.justification: The revision adds Section 3.6, locally expands related work and architectural explanations, and edits wording, heading capitalization and conference front matter. Most prose and the overall section and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: The combined accuracy-FLOPs plot in v1 Figure 1 becomes a two-panel Figure 5 in the experiments, with separate ViT comparisons and I(ViT) markers. Table 1 gains three rows and moves; other figures are largely retained with resizing and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The I(ViT) control adds useful evidence about representation choices, while Section 3.5 makes the learned-equivariance argument more appropriately conditional. The clearer comparison plot and specific code-release location also help. These are limited gains: the original results and single-run, ImageNet-only evaluation remain unchanged.
